narrative.overview: AdvisorConnect should feel like sitting across from a senior advisor who has done this a thousand times and isn't trying to sell you anything: a private office with a ledger, ink on cotton paper, brass fittings, no gloss. Confidence is expressed through restraint and precision, not enthusiasm. This system explicitly rejects the generic navy/sky-blue/orange SaaS-fintech look the codebase shipped with, the warm cream AI-generated default, the black-and-gold luxury-banking cliche, and growth-hacky urgency patterns.
keyCharacteristics: Paper-white and near-black ink carry the exacting read; oxblood and pine are sparing and meaningful.
Borders do the structural work; shadows are reserved for modals, dropdowns, and toasts.
Serif headlines over a neutral grotesque body (Inter).
Status must be readable at a glance across client, advisor, and admin surfaces.

rules.name: The One Fill Rule
rules.body: Oxblood and Pine each appear as a solid fill in exactly one context class. Everywhere else they show up as text, border, or icon color.

rules.name: The Serif-Never-Shouts Rule
rules.body: Source Serif 4 is used at 500 weight only, never bold, never above the display clamp ceiling.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow on anything still inside document flow is a bug, not a style choice.

dos: Do use Oxblood as a solid fill only for primary buttons, active nav state, and the user's own chat bubbles.
Do use Pine exclusively for verified/approved/confirmed states.
Do keep body text at Ink or Muted, never a paler gray.
Do use 1px hairline borders as the default separator.
Do reserve shadows for modals, dropdowns, popovers, and toasts only.
donts: Don't revive the navy/sky-blue/orange-CTA palette or anything generic SaaS-fintech-blue.
Don't use a warm cream/beige/sand background.
Don't reach for a black-and-gold luxury-banking treatment.
Don't add countdown urgency, gradient hero text, or confetti to booking/financial flows.
Don't put a drop shadow on anything inside normal document flow.
Don't use Danger red and Oxblood interchangeably.
